[7] GitHub Issue #466: "[BUG] Context already been set."
https://github.com/boxed/mutmut/issues/466
State: OPEN. Root cause: `set_start_method('fork')` at module level re-executes when `python -m mutmut run` triggers a re-import of `mutmut.__main__` (not cached in `sys.modules`). Fix proposed: guard with `get_start_method(allow_none=True) is None`. Affects Python 3.12, 3.13, 3.14. Not Python-version-specific.

[8] GitHub Issue #486: "mutmut v3 copies source to temp dir, breaking editable-install imports."
https://github.com/boxed/mutmut/issues/486
State: OPEN. No maintainer response. Reports `ModuleNotFoundError` when using `pip install -e .` with src/ layout. Editable install .pth file points to original source, not mutants/ copy.

[9] GitHub Issue #387: "mutmut 3.3.0 does not mutate decorated functions/methods."
https://github.com/boxed/mutmut/issues/387
State: OPEN. Collaborator confirmed: `file_mutation.py` line 175 skips ALL decorated functions. Applies to `@typechecked`, `@staticmethod`, `@classmethod`, `@pytest.mark.*`, `@app.post()`, etc. Proposed fix: allow/deny list or restructured trampoline that keeps decorator on wrapper only.

[10] GitHub Issue #456: "Mutation testing doesn't work with Django app structure."
https://github.com/boxed/mutmut/issues/456
State: OPEN. `paths_to_mutate` must point to all source code, not just the target file. Tests fail because mutmut runs pytest from `mutants/` directory and relative paths break.

[11] GitHub Issue #341: "All the statuses become 'not checked'."
https://github.com/boxed/mutmut/issues/341
State: OPEN. Root cause: `pytest.ini` not copied to `mutants/`. Fix: add `also_copy=pytest.ini`. Now added to default `also_copy` list on main branch.

## Python Documentation (Tier 1)

[12] Python 3.13 multiprocessing documentation — `set_start_method()` and `get_start_method()`.
https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/multiprocessing.html
Extracted: `set_start_method()` raises `RuntimeError` if already set and `force` is not `True`. Should be called at most once, inside `if __name__ == '__main__'`. `get_start_method(allow_none=True)` returns `None` if not explicitly set.

[13] PEP 499: "python -m module reimport problem."
https://peps.python.org/pep-0499/
Status: Deferred. Describes the dual-instance problem when `python -m` executes a module: the module is bound to `sys.modules['__main__']` but not to its canonical name, so subsequent imports re-execute it.
